RISK MANAGEMENT PROGRAM - EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
1. Accidental Release Prevention and Emergency Response Policies
At the DRT America, Inc. (DRT) Rincon, Georgia chemical manufacturing facility (Facility), methyl mercaptan is stored in a quantity above the United States Environmental Protection Agency (USEPA) threshold for Risk Management Program applicability.  Methyl mercaptan is an impurity in crude sulfate turpentine (CST), a raw material of the production process.  The quantity of methyl mercaptan stored at the plant makes it necessary to observe certain safety precautions in handling to prevent unnecessary human exposure, to reduce the threat to personal health maintenance workers, and to reduce the threat to members of nearby community and the environment. It is the policy of the DRT to adhere to applicable federal and state rules and regulations. DRTs accidental release prevention program involves a unified approach that integrates technologies, procedures, and management practices. DRT's emergency preparedness and response plan includes written procedures for reacting to events associated with spills at the Facility. The procedures include safe handling procedures, mitigation techniques, and communication protocols (internal and external).
2. Regulated Substances Handled
The regulated substance handled at the DRT facility is methyl mercaptan. Methyl mercaptan is stored in two 83,813-gallon tanks, one 44,017-gallon tank, and two 3,000-gallon trucks at the Facility. The methyl mercaptan at the Facility is found in CST at concentrations ranging from 0.2% to 5.0% by volume. Storage tanks containing CST are equipped with nitrogen blanketing systems to reduce oxygen levels in the vapor space, minimizing fire and explosion risks and limiting methyl mercaptan emissions. Vapors containing methyl mercaptan are typically routed from the tank farm and downstream process units to a thermal oxidizer, where they are safely destroyed through high-temperature combustion.
